relevance_note: The paper describes one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant and gives individual-level clinical detail: 'A monoallelic loss of TNFAIP3 was caused by a heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion in patient-191 (Fig. 1b).'
method_note: Read the whole Markdown file, including the converted online supplement. The paper is a CNV cohort (191 patients with suspected IEI); only patient-191 carries a TNFAIP3 variant, so patient-191 is the only in-scope person. All other CNV/SNV carriers (ICOS, UBE2T, CORO1A, FANCA, TYK2, 22q11.2, ATM, CD19/LAT, TRAC/SLC7A7/CEBPE, MEFV, CYBA, PSTPIP1, LRBA, TRIM22, BRIP1, IKBKG and the SNV carriers DOCK2/PIK3R1/NFKB1/NFKB2/NLRC4) are out of scope; their number is covered by cohort_size_as_stated. Table 1 appears in this conversion only as its heading and legend (no table body), and Tab.S1/Tab.S2 are images, so no row was taken from a table. patient-005 (previously reported in 2003) is an ICOS patient and out of scope, but the re-report statement is recorded in publications. is_proband is false with span null: the paper never uses a proband or index-case wording for patient-191 and the paper is a cohort, not a case report. disease_label_as_stated is 'not reported' because the authors give this person only 'another conclusive molecular diagnosis', no disease name. Rosacea was mapped to the checklist item 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)'; pulmonary emphysema and chronic sinusitis match no checklist item and only appear in phenotypic_features. No stacked ' / ' cells were encountered, and no contradictions inside the paper were found. Every span was checked programmatically against the paper text.
